arrival_intent: Compare this engineering decision with choices I have faced in my own systems.
background: A practising engineer who knows the tools but not this team's constraints.
desired_payoff: A mechanism or trade-off I can argue with or adapt, even if I would choose differently.
drawn_in_by: The concrete shape of the problem, alternatives that were genuinely available, and what the result changed.
put_off_by: A victory lap that hides cost, or implementation detail without the decision it served.

arrival_intent: Test the author's claims and, if they are weak, catch the slip.
background: A senior engineer with enough scar tissue to distrust tidy engineering stories, but enough curiosity to keep checking.
desired_payoff: To push on the argument and, if it holds, grudgingly admit that the author knows what he is talking about.
drawn_in_by: Falsifiable detail, counterpressure, and limits stated before I have to supply them myself.
put_off_by: Borrowed authority, unearned certainty, or a convenient omission that makes the result look inevitable.

arrival_intent: Decide whether this person is worth a longer conversation.
background: Reviewing several portfolios with limited time; technically literate but unfamiliar with this project.
desired_payoff: A credible instance of ownership, judgement, and consequence I can remember after closing the tab.
drawn_in_by: A clear stake early on and specifics that reveal what the author personally noticed or decided.
put_off_by: Long setup before the point, inflated impact claims, or a team achievement presented as a solo rescue.

arrival_intent: Learn why this problem matters without already knowing the system.
background: Comfortable with software ideas, new to the article's particular technology or domain.
desired_payoff: Enough context to follow the decision and explain its significance in my own words.
drawn_in_by: Terms introduced when needed and examples that let me build a mental picture.
put_off_by: Acronyms or internal history treated as common knowledge, or basic concepts explained at exhausting length.

arrival_intent: See whether this lesson would survive contact with my existing codebase.
background: Responsible for old systems, migration risk, operational load, and the next engineer's working day.
desired_payoff: A boundary, warning, or practical sequence I could use without pretending my constraints disappear.
drawn_in_by: Failure modes, reversibility, and the awkward middle between stopping harm and fixing it properly.
put_off_by: Clean-slate advice, omitted migration costs, or a fix that merely moves the burden elsewhere.

arrival_intent: Assess how the author made a decision under delivery and team pressure.
background: Accountable for technical direction while balancing people, time, and business consequences.
desired_payoff: A decision process I could defend to both engineers and stakeholders.
drawn_in_by: Visible priorities, trade-offs, who bore the risk, and why the timing of the decision mattered.
put_off_by: Architecture as an end in itself or commercial pressure used as a vague excuse.

arrival_intent: Reconstruct the failure and see how it was contained.
background: Has debugged production incidents and knows early theories are often wrong.
desired_payoff: A causal chain from symptom to mechanism, including what bought time before the durable fix.
drawn_in_by: Evidence at each turn, discarded hypotheses, and the operational effect of the immediate action.
put_off_by: A mystery reveal that withholds useful facts for drama, or a root cause asserted without proof.

arrival_intent: Read an engineering story for the pleasure of how it is told as well as what it teaches.
background: Reads technical essays and notices pacing, scenes, and whether the author's voice feels inhabited.
desired_payoff: A progression that makes the technical turn and the ending feel earned.
drawn_in_by: A live question, precise scenes, and changes in understanding rather than repeated summaries.
put_off_by: Stock drama, decorative jokes, or a moral stapled onto a story that already made its point.

arrival_intent: Find the circumstances under which the apparent lesson would fail.
background: Has watched useful local solutions harden into bad universal advice.
desired_payoff: A claim with an honest domain of validity, not a rule that collapses at the first counterexample.
drawn_in_by: Explicit assumptions, competing explanations, and exceptions that sharpen rather than erase the point.
put_off_by: Universal language drawn from one case or a counterexample dismissed without engaging its mechanism.

arrival_intent: Imagine what it would be like to solve a hard problem with this author.
background: A potential colleague who values candour and shared ownership more than polished heroics.
desired_payoff: Signals that this person can reason openly, change course, and give others credit.
drawn_in_by: The author's role made clear, colleagues' contributions visible, and mistakes treated as information.
put_off_by: Blame shifted onto absent teammates or a flawless-protagonist account of collaborative work.

arrival_intent: Work out how an experienced engineer recognised what mattered in an unfamiliar problem.
background: An early-career engineer who has learned techniques but has had fewer chances to own consequential decisions.
desired_payoff: A reasoning move I can practise, with enough context to see why it was chosen.
drawn_in_by: The observations that changed the author's mind and the questions asked before committing to a fix.
put_off_by: A magic-sounding instinct with no intermediate reasoning, or an unexplained wall of local jargon.

arrival_intent: Decide whether I could try this practice on my own team without creating a second job.
background: A working engineer with delivery responsibilities and limited authority to redesign the team's workflow.
desired_payoff: A modest first move, its prerequisites, and a way to tell whether it helped.
drawn_in_by: Specific setup costs, failure signals, and changes small enough to try beside existing work.
put_off_by: A transformation story that assumes spare time, full autonomy, or a team already convinced.

arrival_intent: Test whether the local decision respects system boundaries and survives a wider rollout.
background: An architect accountable for several systems and for the exceptions that appear at scale.
desired_payoff: A clear statement of where the approach holds, where it bends, and who owns the boundary.
drawn_in_by: Alternatives, coupling, reversibility, and evidence that the local win did not create distant cost.
put_off_by: A design proclaimed generally correct from one team or one incident.

arrival_intent: Judge whether the proposed agent or engineering practice makes a shared project easier to maintain.
background: A maintainer who handles issue triage, review, contributor guidance, and long-lived compatibility.
desired_payoff: A practice that improves contribution quality without shifting unseen work onto maintainers.
drawn_in_by: Reviewable changes, clear provenance, restrained automation, and explicit upkeep.
put_off_by: A throughput claim that counts generated contributions but ignores review and support load.

arrival_intent: See what a team would need from the platform to run this agentic workflow safely.
background: Builds shared paths for developers while managing identity, deployment, observability, and policy.
desired_payoff: A concrete platform boundary and an adoption route that can serve more than one team.
drawn_in_by: Ownership of credentials, execution scope, resource limits, and developer experience.
put_off_by: A local prototype presented as deployable without showing the platform work it depends on.

arrival_intent: Assess what happens to service reliability after the clever solution goes live.
background: Operates production services and pays attention to capacity, alerting, rollback, and on-call burden.
desired_payoff: A credible account of steady-state operation and how failure will be detected and recovered.
drawn_in_by: Runtime limits, observability, incident history, and what changed for the person on call.
put_off_by: A successful deployment treated as proof that the system is now reliable.

arrival_intent: Find the test that could make the author's confidence fail before production does.
background: Designs tests around risky assumptions, integration boundaries, and misleading green signals.
desired_payoff: An explicit claim, its strongest falsifying check, and what a failure would change.
drawn_in_by: Test selection tied to a specific risk, with observed results and acknowledged blind spots.
put_off_by: A large test count used as a substitute for showing what was actually put at risk.

arrival_intent: Understand the authority granted to agents and the paths by which an attacker could misuse it.
background: Reviews software permissions, data flows, untrusted inputs, and third-party integrations.
desired_payoff: A bounded threat picture with controls proportionate to the actual capabilities.
drawn_in_by: Trust boundaries, permission scope, auditability, and a realistic misuse case.
put_off_by: A safety claim based on good intentions or a prompt while tool access remains broad.

arrival_intent: Decide whether the claimed agent behaviour was measured in a way I could reproduce or challenge.
background: Builds evaluations for model-assisted workflows and expects variation across inputs and runs.
desired_payoff: A clear task, baseline, failure criteria, and evidence that the observed improvement generalises enough for its use.
drawn_in_by: Representative cases, negative controls, decision traces, and attention to regression.
put_off_by: One impressive demonstration promoted into a general capability claim.

arrival_intent: Check what information the workflow reads, sends, retains, and exposes.
background: Responsible for data handling across tools, vendors, logs, and operational processes.
desired_payoff: A data-flow boundary I could explain and assess without guessing where content travelled.
drawn_in_by: Named inputs and outputs, retention, consent or authority, and limits on secondary use.
put_off_by: A description that says data is safe without specifying where it goes.

arrival_intent: Decide whether this practice changes team outcomes enough to justify its organisational cost.
background: Responsible for multiple teams, capability development, delivery health, and uneven adoption.
desired_payoff: Evidence of where the practice helps, what conditions it needs, and what managers must support.
drawn_in_by: Team-level effects, training burden, failure patterns, and signs of healthy adoption.
put_off_by: Personal productivity anecdotes presented as organisational transformation.

arrival_intent: See whether this engineering choice is proportionate for a small team with little slack.
background: Owns technical risk and business survival while still close enough to inspect implementation.
desired_payoff: A practical decision that protects the product without building a platform before it is needed.
drawn_in_by: Costs, sequencing, reversibility, and the point at which a more elaborate solution becomes justified.
put_off_by: Enterprise ceremony with no small-team payoff, or speed celebrated without reckoning with risk.

arrival_intent: Understand which user or business problem the engineering decision actually changed.
background: Shapes priorities with engineers and must explain why a technical investment deserves time.
desired_payoff: A visible line from constraint to decision to user or business consequence.
drawn_in_by: The user journey affected, the trade-off accepted, and evidence of the resulting change.
put_off_by: Technical sophistication presented as value without an outcome anyone outside engineering can name.

arrival_intent: Look for the human behaviour and context that the technical account might have missed.
background: Studies how people use products and how teams interpret evidence about those users.
desired_payoff: A credible account of whose needs were observed and which assumptions remain untested.
drawn_in_by: Specific users, observed friction, and a willingness to revise the technical framing.
put_off_by: A user benefit inferred solely from system metrics or an imagined happy path.

arrival_intent: Determine whether the solution's recurring cost is visible and accountable.
background: Works across engineering and finance on variable cloud and AI spending.
desired_payoff: A cost model that distinguishes experiment, scale, and ongoing operation.
drawn_in_by: Unit costs, workload shape, ownership of spend, and the trade-off against alternatives.
put_off_by: Cheap single-call prices used to dismiss aggregate use, waste, or unpredictable demand.

arrival_intent: Assess whether a tool or provider claim is strong enough to inform a buying decision.
background: Reviews supplier evidence, operating costs, contractual exposure, and organisational fit.
desired_payoff: A question set and evidence trail for deciding whether adoption is justified.
drawn_in_by: Measured capability, data handling, lock-in, support model, and failure conditions.
put_off_by: Vendor language repeated as evidence or an internal experiment treated as a purchasing case.

arrival_intent: Find a concise, defensible signal to bring to a hiring manager.
background: Sources engineering candidates but cannot personally validate every technical detail.
desired_payoff: A memorable account of scope, ownership, and judgement that I can accurately relay.
drawn_in_by: Clear role and outcome language backed by concrete examples.
put_off_by: Dense internal terminology or a story that never states what the candidate personally did.

arrival_intent: Find a case that helps learners practise engineering judgement rather than memorise a rule.
background: Teaches or mentors software engineers and looks for authentic decisions with discussable alternatives.
desired_payoff: A teachable dilemma whose constraints, evidence, and consequences support more than one initial answer.
drawn_in_by: Moments where a reader can pause, choose, then compare their reasoning with the author's.
put_off_by: A tidy moral that erases the uncertainty students need to grapple with.

arrival_intent: See what senior engineering work looks like beyond writing code.
background: Has related professional experience and is learning the language and responsibilities of software teams.
desired_payoff: A concrete picture of the decisions, collaboration, and accountability involved.
drawn_in_by: Human stakes, explained concepts, and links between technical choices and work practices.
put_off_by: Acronyms and status signals that make the role sound like a closed club.

arrival_intent: Understand how engineering constraints and visual judgement shaped the finished work.
background: Arrived through a design, typography, or visual-story article rather than an agentic engineering search.
desired_payoff: A specific creative decision and its effect on what a visitor can see or understand.
drawn_in_by: References used with discernment, production constraints, and honest account of what changed.
put_off_by: Design described only as decoration or technical implementation offered in place of aesthetic reasoning.

arrival_intent: Make sense of a widely discussed engineering or AI claim without becoming an engineer first.
background: Follows technology because it affects work or culture and is willing to learn a useful mechanism.
desired_payoff: An explanation I can retell accurately, including where the claim stops.
drawn_in_by: A concrete situation, ordinary-language stakes, and terms introduced only when needed.
put_off_by: Acronyms doing the argument's work or hype that asks for belief before explanation.

arrival_intent: Decide whether this lesson is useful and accurate enough to share with practitioners.
background: Explains technical practices publicly and is alert to examples that travel badly out of context.
desired_payoff: A portable insight with its conditions attached and a credible example to point to.
drawn_in_by: Clear teaching structure, source links, boundary cases, and a claim sized to its evidence.
put_off_by: A catchy slogan that outruns the implementation or conceals a sharp edge.

arrival_intent: Check whether an engineering account respects the rules and consequences of the domain it serves.
background: Knows the operational or business domain deeply but does not need to know every software component.
desired_payoff: Confidence that the technical decision preserved the domain distinctions that matter.
drawn_in_by: Real cases, exceptions, user obligations, and a trace from domain rule to system behaviour.
put_off_by: Domain complexity flattened into a convenient toy example.

arrival_intent: See whether a local solution survives the boundaries between teams, services, and suppliers.
background: Connects existing systems under contractual, technical, and migration constraints.
desired_payoff: A sequence for adoption that makes dependencies and ownership visible.
drawn_in_by: Interface assumptions, failure handling, cutover plans, and how an old system coexists with the new.
put_off_by: A greenfield example offered as though integration work were incidental.
